tts_summary:
Good morning. Here is your market briefing for Monday September 21st.

We are kicking off the week with an unexpected risk-on move. S&P futures are up 49 points, about 65 basis points. Nasdaq is leading with gains of 110 basis points. Asia closed broadly higher — Hang Seng up over 1 percent, Korea up 1.65 percent. Europe is up 85 to 120 basis points with data center infrastructure names outperforming. Treasuries have a bid, yields down 2 to 3 basis points across the curve.

Here is what makes this morning's strength confounding: almost every piece of weekend news was negative. The Houthis launched a brazen missile and drone attack on Saudi Arabia. Ukraine initiated its largest drone strike of the war against Russia. AI headlines out of Friday afternoon were a mess — Anthropic's IPO is delayed, its 2027 ARR projections disappointed investors, OpenAI is projecting roughly 280 billion dollars in negative free cash flow through 2030, and Oracle's data center debt tied to a New Mexico facility called Project Jupiter has hit a wall with lenders.

So what is driving the rally? One word: diplomacy. The UN General Assembly runs September 22nd through the 28th in New York, and Trump over the weekend signaled he would be open to meeting with Iran's president. He also pulled back from authorizing air strikes against the Houthis at the last minute Sunday night. The market is betting that even a small improvement in Middle East tensions could trigger a sharp drop in oil — and if oil falls sustainably, you get lower yields, less hawkish monetary policy, better margins, and a consumer confidence boost all at once. Brent is already sliding today, down 170 basis points to around 102 dollars.

On the company side, a few names to flag. Novo Nordisk is getting hit in European trading after failing to provide specific financial targets at its analyst meeting today — investors wanted numbers and did not get them. Oracle faces fresh pressure after a Financial Times report detailed lender resistance to loans tied to its massive New Mexico data center — another reminder that off-balance sheet AI commitments across Big Tech have surged roughly 300 billion dollars in the last year. Disney's parks business is a relative bright spot, outperforming theme park peers through pricing promotions and package deals. And Nscale, a London-based neocloud company, has filed its S1 and plans to list on the New York Stock Exchange — though the timing into a choppy AI infrastructure tape is worth watching.

On the Fed and rates — policy globally is still pointed hawkish. The three biggest central banks all hiked this month. Kansas City Fed President Schmid and Minneapolis Fed President Kashkari both warned over the weekend that inflation is broad-based, not just an oil story. Markets are pricing about 33 basis points of additional hikes over the final two Fed meetings, with roughly even odds on October 28th.

The key watch item for this week is the Trump-Xi summit on Thursday, which could deliver modest tariff reductions on around 30 billion dollars worth of goods. But the bigger macro swing factor is Iran. The UN General Assembly is the best diplomatic opportunity the market has had in months. If something moves there, the oil trade unwinds fast and everything else follows. If it disappoints, the bear case reasserts quickly — energy costs are already filtering into corporate margins and consumer wallets, and the demand destruction has not fully shown up in the data yet. Nothing major on today's calendar. Stay focused on geopolitical headlines out of New York.
